title.narrative: A thriving Kenyan digital platforms’ ecosystem that advances sustainable development and leaves no one behind

description.narrative: DigiKen aims to foster a thriving Kenyan digital platforms’ ecosystem that advances sustainable development and leaves no one behind. With gender equality and environmental sustainability mainstreamed throughout all activities, DigiKen’s objectives are closely aligned with Kenya’s country priorities, as outlined in the Kenya Vision 2030, to become “a newly industrialising, middle-income country providing a high quality of life to all its citizens by 2030 in a clean and secure environment”. The results arising from DigiKen’s digital platform ecosystem-building will channel catalytic impacts across three SDG Transitions: Towards Digital Transformation, it will distribute the benefits of digital transformation to all people in Kenya at risk of left behind, by empowering LNOB groups with media and information literacy, and digital skills to engage with digital platforms. Towards Decent Jobs and Universal Social Protection, it will generate employment opportunities — especially for youth and women — through much-needed private sector growth and investment in digital platform technologies. Finally, towards Climate, Biodiversity and Pollution, it will leverage partnership with the existing green Digital Innovation Hub (gDIH) and support digital platforms that will mainstream sustainability from design principles and deliver effective solutions to local challenges. The joint programme will leverage on four engine rooms: shifting policy regulatory framework towards the growth of digital platform economy and implementation of governance framework, capacity building at scale of Government and public sector officials, developing market ready pipelines, and devising a financing mix to enable MSMEs, local start-ups, and entrepreneurs to access to capital and invest in digital platforms. Estimated number of Kenyans impacted by the end of the Joint Programme is over 2 million and the leverage of funding/financing is US$ 55 million.
